content:
maria-ops: Heads-up — Aurora Health (Dedicated) is seeing p95 spikes on small, bursty requests. They say it started after last runtime deploy. Asking for a per-customer batch/queue token_budget recommendation.
kevin-ml: Can you paste a quick profile and the model + quant info?
maria-ops: model: rwd-v3-7b-quant, docker runtime tag: r-infer:2025-02-28, observed kernel fallback pattern. Quick profile below.
maria-ops: ```
[PROFILE] 2025-03-02T10:12:45Z
model: rwd-v3-7b-q
kernel_switches: fused_attn -> generic_attn (count=42 over 2m)
kv_cache_hit_rate: 13%
avg_tokens_per_batch: 6
batch_formation_delay_ms: 24
p50_latency_ms: 48
p95_latency_ms: 312
notes: many short requests cause small batches, selector pads then selects generic path
```
devon-runtime: This looks like the kernel-selector heuristic change in PR#3490 — it started favoring padded batch alignment for throughput which can flip to generic_attn for short seqs. That's likely the regression.
devon-runtime: For Dedicated we can tune token_budget and queue limits per customer to avoid pathological padding and keep the fused kernels engaged.
samir-sre: Suggestion for Aurora can be conservative to start: token_budget_per_queue=1500, max_queue_size=48, batch_window_ms=12, min_batch_tokens=8. Also enable kv_cache_affinity=sticky so repeated callers land on same worker and improve hit_rate. :thumbsup: 
jenna-eng: I'll open a canary with those settings on dedicated-aurora pool and add a short windowed rollout (5% -> 25% -> 100%), monitor p95 and kernel switch counts. If p95 doesn't drop under 250ms we roll back.
kevin-ml: Two follow-ups: 1) add a small eval that simulates KV-miss heavy workload so we can detect regressions in CI; 2) add a metric alert on `kernel_switches.to_generic / minute` and `kv_cache_hit_rate` per-customer.
maria-ops: Agree. Also customer asked for explicit per-customer queue_limit so they can cap concurrency from their side. We should give them recommended client-side rate limits: concurrent_requests <= 30, tokens_per_minute <= 40000 (temporary).
perf-bot: canary rollout started (canary_id=aurora-2025-03-02-15:01Z). Link: https://console/redwood/canaries/aurora-2025-03-02
maria-ops: Thanks team. If canary looks good, I'll coordinate an SLA note with Aurora and schedule a post-mortem doc. Also adding an eval prompt set specifically to trip KV-cache miss cases.
jenna-eng: Logged runbook: revert PR#3490 -> runtime-config token_budget fallback -> notify Aurora. I'll post progress here.
kevin-ml: If we keep kv_cache_affinity sticky, watch for hotspotting on specific GPUs — set soft-evict policy if memory > 85%.
samir-sre: noted. I'll make the eviction threshold explicit in the canary config.
maria-ops: Great. Closing loop once we have 1h of canary metrics. :white_check_mark:
